questions.text: An ionic bond forms between two atoms when ____.

options.text: one atom transfers electrons to another, creating oppositely charged ions
two atoms share electrons equally between them in a bonding pair
two atoms share electrons unequally due to electronegativity difference
a metal atom accepts electrons donated by a non-metal atom

questions.explanation: Ionic bonds form through electron TRANSFER (not sharing): a metal atom donates electrons to a non-metal, forming a cation (+) and anion (−) which attract electrostatically. Option B describes a pure covalent bond; Option C describes a polar covalent bond. Option D reverses the direction — metals DONATE, non-metals ACCEPT electrons.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds contains a covalent bond?

options.text: NaCl — sodium chloride (table salt)
H₂O — water molecule (two H-O bonds)
MgO — magnesium oxide used in refractory bricks
CaCl₂ — calcium chloride used as drying agent

questions.explanation: H₂O has covalent O-H bonds (oxygen and hydrogen SHARE electrons). NaCl, MgO, and CaCl₂ are all ionic compounds (metal + non-metal → electron transfer). A quick rule: non-metal + non-metal = covalent; metal + non-metal = ionic.

questions.text: Ionic compounds generally have high melting points because ____.

options.text: strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions requires high energy to overcome
their covalent electron-sharing bonds are extremely short and very strong
their molecules are held together by weak London dispersion forces throughout
the delocalized electron sea in their lattice provides strong metallic bonding

questions.explanation: In an ionic lattice, each ion is surrounded by multiple oppositely charged ions — the sum of all electrostatic attractions (Coulombic forces) is very strong. Breaking this lattice requires a large amount of energy → high melting point (e.g., NaCl mp = 801°C). Option D describes metallic bonding (metals), not ionic compounds.

questions.text: A double bond (as in ethylene C₂H₄) consists of ____.

options.text: one sigma (σ) bond and one pi (π) bond between the two carbons
two sigma (σ) bonds and no pi bonds between the carbons
one pi (π) bond only, with no sigma bond present
two pi (π) bonds and one sigma bond between the carbons

questions.explanation: A double bond = 1 sigma (σ) + 1 pi (π) bond. The σ bond forms by head-on orbital overlap (allows free rotation in single bonds). The π bond forms by lateral p-orbital overlap (restricts rotation in double bonds → cis/trans isomerism). A triple bond = 1σ + 2π.

questions.text: The water molecule (H₂O) has a bent shape rather than a linear shape because ____.

options.text: the two lone pairs on oxygen repel the bonding pairs, reducing the bond angle
the two hydrogen atoms repel each other strongly across the molecule
oxygen forms weaker bonds with hydrogen than with other non-metals
the sp³ hybrid orbitals on each hydrogen atom cause the bending observed

questions.explanation: VSEPR theory: the two lone pairs on oxygen repel the two O-H bonding pairs more strongly than bonding pairs repel each other. This forces the H-O-H bond angle below the tetrahedral 109.5° to ~104.5°, creating the characteristic bent shape. Lone pair-lone pair repulsion > lone pair-bond pair repulsion > bond pair-bond pair repulsion.

questions.text: Diamond and graphite are both allotropes of carbon. Diamond is hard and non-conducting; graphite is soft and conducts electricity. This difference arises because ____.

options.text: diamond has sp³ 3D covalent lattice; graphite has sp² layers with delocalised π electrons
diamond has ionic bonding; graphite has metallic bonding with free electrons
diamond has only σ bonds; graphite has only π bonds throughout its structure
diamond is a polymer while graphite consists of discrete C₆₀ fullerene molecules

questions.explanation: Diamond: each carbon is sp³ hybridised, bonded to 4 others in a rigid 3D tetrahedral lattice → extremely hard, no free electrons → non-conductor. Graphite: each carbon is sp² hybridised, bonded to 3 in layers, with one delocalised π electron per carbon → conducts electricity, layers slide easily (soft/lubricant). Both are purely covalent — option B is wrong.

questions.text: Hydrogen bonding is a special type of dipole-dipole interaction. Which condition is necessary for hydrogen bonding to occur?

options.text: Hydrogen must be covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom (F, O, or N)
Hydrogen must be bonded to a metal atom in an ionic crystal structure
Hydrogen must be the central atom surrounded by more electronegative ligands
The molecule must be completely non-polar with symmetrical electron cloud

questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding requires: H covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom (F, O, or N). The large electronegativity difference makes the H highly δ+ and the electronegative atom highly δ−, allowing the δ+ H to attract a lone pair on another F/O/N atom. This explains water's anomalously high boiling point (100°C vs expected ~−80°C for its molecular mass).
